cohort: The study participants were 250 mothers who underwent delivery in a tertiary care hospital in Pakistan.
finding: The study found a high cesarean section rate of 44% in the study population, significantly influenced by younger maternal age, education level, urban residence, medical conditions (preeclampsia/eclampsia, vaginal hemorrhage, gestational diabetes, hypertension), and preterm gestational age.
mod_finding: A high cesarean section rate (44%) was observed, influenced by maternal age, education level, medical risk factors, urban residence, and preterm gestational age.
cross-section timing: During delivery at a tertiary care hospital
